decisions.executionNote: Approach the left-side tube with the left arm, raising into an elbow-up arc and beginning downward grasp orientation.
Advance above the left tube while aligning the gripper to its visible axis; keep right arm parked.
Lower toward the left tube with the gripper open, finishing alignment to its horizontal axis.
Fine-align the left gripper to the tube, then close fully for a retention check.
Lift the closed left gripper clear of the table and inspect whether the tube remains between the fingers.
Tube appears retained. Rotate it gradually toward upright while translating toward the left rack slot.
Finish uprighting the retained tube above the left portion of the rack; keep a clearance before insertion.
Align over the visible left-front large slot and begin a slow vertical insertion, retaining the tube.
Lower the upright left tube into the aligned rack opening, stopping near the demonstrated insertion height before releasing.
Ease slight rim contact with a small inward correction, then release to inspect whether the first tube seats upright.
Withdraw the open left gripper without dragging the tube and inspect its seating and uprightness.
First tube is not upright after release. Clear the rack with the open gripper to see its resting pose before recovery.
Return above the leaning first tube with open fingers for a controlled regrasp rather than treating it as seated.
Lower open fingers around the exposed upper portion of the leaning tube and close for recovery.
Lift the regrasped tube clear of the rack to assess its new orientation and avoid rotating against the slot.
The regrasp retains the tube near its cap. Tilt the wrist gradually to bring the tube axis upright while keeping it above the rack.
Continue slowly uprighting the recovered tube and bring its lower end over the left rack opening.
Make a small axis and tip-alignment correction above the left-front slot, then lower cautiously.
Center the visible tube tip over the large left-front opening and lower in small increments.
Advance the recovered tube vertically into the opening while holding its current near-upright alignment.
Correct the visible tube lean with a small pivot above the opening, easing pressure instead of forcing it downward.
Tube axis now appears closer to upright. Lower gently through the aligned opening, watching for renewed rim contact.
Release the tube without additional pressure and withdraw to determine whether it settles into the opening.
Clear the first tube for settling and begin an elbow-up approach to the inner right-side tube with the right arm.
Advance the right gripper toward the inner tube with its fingers aligned across the tube; retreat the left arm along an elbow-up path.
Lower the right gripper around the inner tube with axis alignment; finish parking the left arm without crossing workspaces.
Replan from the continuity stop with smaller left-arm increments. Finish right-tube alignment and close the right gripper.
Lift the inner right tube clear of the table while keeping the gripper closed; verify retention before rotating.
The right tube is retained. Rotate it toward upright while carrying it toward the right-front rack opening.
Finish rotating the second tube upright above the right rack slot, keeping clearance for visual alignment.
Lower the second tube toward the right-front opening with a small centering adjustment, preserving its upright orientation.
Insert the second tube slowly while keeping the gripper closed and monitoring for rim contact or tube tilt.
Finish the second tube's insertion depth and open the gripper in place to allow the tube to seat without lateral disturbance.
Withdraw from the seated second tube with open fingers and gain clearance for approaching the remaining right-side tube.
Move clear of the rack toward the final right-side tube and begin orienting for a top-down grasp.
After the continuity stop, resume from the observed pose with half-sized translation and rotation increments.
Continue toward the last tube in the right workspace, rotating the open gripper toward the tube's observed axis.
Complete the top-down approach to the final tube, leaving the gripper open until wrist-view alignment can be checked.
Fine-center the right gripper around the final tube, descend the last centimeter, and close for pickup.
Allow the final-tube grasp to settle, then lift without rotating to verify retention and its actual held alignment.
Carry the retained final tube inward through the right workspace, gaining clearance and gradually rotating it toward upright.
Continue transferring the final tube toward the center opening, rotating smoothly and staying above the inserted tubes.
Bring the final tube above the center opening and finish nominal upright alignment, leaving room for visual correction.
Compensate the final tube's visible held tilt and lower toward the center slot cautiously, keeping the tube retained.
Lower the corrected final tube into the center opening in small vertical increments, monitoring its alignment.
The final tube appears to have met the rim rather than descended. Lift clear and make a small centering correction before retrying.
Retry the center opening with a millimeter-scale lateral correction and slow descent, retaining the tube.
Continue the final tube's slow vertical insertion while monitoring whether the tube follows the gripper without renewed rim contact.
Ease the apparent center-slot rim contact, shift the retained tube slightly farther into the rack, and retry a short descent.
Release the final tube without pressing further, and withdraw slightly to inspect its resting position and the slot alignment.
The final tube is tilted rather than seated. Regrasp its exposed body for lifting and alignment to the large center opening.
